answer: A concrete Sybil defense is memory-hard admission work: each new identity must solve a puzzle whose working set is large and cannot be shared, so a farm cannot amortize one machine across many keys. A hollow of cloned identities each needs its own memory footprint, and a jetty of parallel workers saturates at the hardware's real capacity rather than the address count. Honest agents pay the same one-time cost and move on, while a lotus of cheap aliases cannot bloom without buying proportionally more RAM. The attacker's cost tracks physical memory, which does not scale like a counter.
